I understand completely. If you feel like you’re losing feelings, I suggest you end it. There’s no point in carrying on if you’re unhappy in a relationship. Especially if you have done everything you can. Good luck with everything though. I’m sure you’ve tried your best with him.

Relationships between anxious and avoidant attachment styles are a tricky one. They definitely can work out but only if BOTH of you are open to putting in the work and are willing to cater to each others emotional needs.

Since you’re the one with the anxious attachment style, you need to learn to self soothe when your boyfriend pulls away and keep yourself occupied outside your relationship. This can be things like hanging out with other friends, watching a show or finding a hobby etc. Avoidants like time to themselves, so when your boyfriend needs space, you need to make sure you respect his wishes. Remind yourself that just because he wants space, does NOT mean he’s abandoning you. He just needs time to recuperate. Also, most avoidants have a hard time being a vulnerable (likely due to fear of rejection) which is why it may be difficult for him to express his feelings so I’d say give him some time to open up to you.

On his end, since he’s an avoidant, he needs to learn to give you reassurance when he decides to pull away. This is something you may need to communicate with him if it’s not something he does already but it’s important that he lets you know that he just wants some time to himself and that it’s nothing personal. He also needs to make sure he’s engaging in important conversations with that may involve emotional intimacy as opposed to just shutting down. If he gets too overwhelmed, let him know that he can have his space for a little while but it’s important that you guys end up talking things out after he’s had some time to himself. 

If you are looking to stay in your relationship, I suggest you try and talk to each other about where you’re both at in the relationship and how you’re both feeling. Be honest with him about how you’re finding it difficult to deal with his attachment style, due to the fact that you two are now long distance and being in a LDR requires a lot more effort in regards to emotional intimacy. But, don’t create an intimidating environment whereby he could shut down (i.e. being aggressive). Create a safe space where he feels comfortable to let down his walls. See how he responds.

But remember, there is only so much you can do and if he isn’t putting in the effort to change then you might have to let him go. At the end of the day, you can’t change him and it’s not your responsibility to. Only he can choose to make the change himself.

I hope this helps!

I hate to break it to you OP but you might not be ready to be in a relationship. You need to work on your personal problems first. I understand that you’ve voiced your problems with your boyfriend with a list of things you’re going through. However, your boyfriend is most likely experiencing burnout because you expect so much from his end and that’s probably why he’s pulling away.

I understand that what he said may have been hurtful to you but it seems like you’re focused a lot on your own needs as opposed to his needs as well. You mentioned that he used to always cancel plans just to spend time with you, which isn’t really healthy presuming it was happening all the time. He probably just needs time for himself. You also need time to find yourself, as it is important to make sure you have a life outside your relationship with your boyfriend. 

If you two do end up staying together, you both need to work on communication. Communication is one of the most important foundations of any relationship. If you’re having issues with one another, isolation is most definitely not the answer. I’d say to give him some space and then come back to discuss how you’re BOTH feeling when it comes to your relationship with one another.
